hypothesis: excel returns descending {3;2;1} (third arg = sort_order, -1=descending); gsheets returns ascending {1;2;3} (third arg = is_ascending, -1 coerces to truthy=ascending). Confirms the SORT third-argument signature divergence.
note: consumes annotation SORT/sort-descending (A4); the sheets.wiki SORT.md documents the gsheets is_ascending signature and would mislead an Excel author.

hypothesis: excel returns {20;30;10} (reorder by ascending rank of by-array keys); gsheets returns #NAME? (SORTBY not exposed in Google Sheets at recording time). Confirms SORTBY is Excel-family-only.
note: consumes annotation SORTBY/sortby-basic (A5); also verify whether current gsheets has since added SORTBY.

hypothesis: excel rejects =AND() at entry as too few arguments (recorded as blank/non-value); gsheets returns #N/A. Confirms whether excel's recorded blank is an entry-rejection artifact rather than a computed value.
note: consumes annotation AND/and-empty (A6); the medium-confidence claim is the excel-blank=entry-rejection interpretation.

hypothesis: excel returns #VALUE!; gsheets returns #NUM!. Confirms the out-of-range CHOOSE error-code split observed in fixtures.
excel returns a blank cell (null); gsheets returns an empty string "". Confirms the blank-vs-empty-string representation split for T of a non-text value.
note: consumes annotation T/t-of-boolean (A12). Distinguishing blank from empty-string is a value-model question the reconciler cares about.

hypothesis: excel and gsheets ignore the quoted-number string literals inside the array constructor (no factors) and return 0, unlike direct scalar args PRODUCT("2","3","4") which would coerce. Confirms the array-literal skip-text rule.
note: consumes annotation A13 (array-literal coercion). Compare with PRODUCT("2","3","4") scalar form if a second probe slot is cheap.

hypothesis: excel and gsheets ignore numbers-stored-as-text in a range and return 0 (vs formulas/hyperformula/ironcalc/lattice which coerce and return 6). Confirms the range skip-text rule with text-typed cells.
note: consumes annotation SUM/sum-of-string-range (A15). Requires the three cells to be seeded as TEXT, not numbers (the divergence vanishes if they are numeric).

hypothesis: excel and gsheets return 0 (booleans inside an array constructor are not coerced), distinct from lattice's 2. Confirms the boolean-array-literal skip rule for excel/gsheets.
note: consumes annotation A13. Contrast with SUM(TRUE,FALSE,TRUE) as scalar args, which Excel coerces to 2.
